_note: Core/Device (parity/F06-device.md), the LAUNCH FOLD: the pure function behind `isFirstLaunch` and `previousVersion`, which are the two values every onboarding flow and every what's-new sheet needs and which existed nowhere in the framework before. Inputs are the version this build reports and the two values persisted from earlier launches; outputs are what to report and what to write back. Keeping it pure is what makes "true exactly once per install" testable without an install. THE RULES: (1) nothing stored at all means a brand new install, so isFirstLaunch is true, previousVersion is absent, and the current version is recorded; (2) the stored version matching the current one is an ordinary relaunch, which reports the previousVersion it already had and WRITES NOTHING (so a second call in the same session cannot change the answer); (3) a differing stored version is an upgrade or a downgrade: it becomes previousVersion, and both keys are rewritten; (4) isFirstLaunch is never true twice, because case 1 writes the version that turns every later launch into case 2 or 3.
_runner: No runner is wired yet (registration is in the F06 handoff). Implemented identically as Device.foldLaunch in swift/, kotlin/ and web/.

fold.name: the very first launch after install
the second launch of the same version is not a first launch, and writes nothing
the first launch after an upgrade reports what was there before
previousVersion survives later launches of the upgraded version
a second upgrade replaces previousVersion rather than chaining it
a downgrade is an upgrade backwards, not a first launch
an empty stored version is a value, not an absence: it is a change, not a first launch
a build with no declared version still folds, and reports one first launch

sequences.name: isFirstLaunch is true exactly once across install, relaunch, upgrade, relaunch
